title: Admissible underlying scheme category of a Stacks big site
statement: Let $S_0$ be a set of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $s(X)$ for the cardinal size of a scheme [def-sfb-scheme-cardinal-size] and $B(\kappa)=\max\{\kappa^{\aleph_0},\kappa^+\}$ for an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, where $\kappa^+$ is its successor cardinal. Write $V_0=\varnothing$, $V_{\beta+1}=\mathcal P(V_\beta)$, and $V_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}V_\beta$ for limit ordinals $\lambda$. Put $\mathit{Sch}_\alpha$ equal to the full category of schemes whose underlying set-theoretic codes belong to $V_\alpha$; full means that its morphisms are all scheme morphisms between its objects. An admissible choice of underlying category for a big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] is $\mathit{Sch}_\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is a limit ordinal satisfying all of the following conditions: (1) $S_0\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathit{Sch}_\alpha)$; (2) for every $S\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathit{Sch}_\alpha)$ and every scheme $W$ with $s(W)\leq B(s(S))$, there exist $S'\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathit{Sch}_\alpha)$ and an isomorphism $W\cong S'$; (3) for any category $I$ with countably many objects and morphisms and any diagram $F:I\to\mathit{Sch}_\alpha$, a limit exists in $\mathit{Sch}_\alpha$ if and only if a limit exists in the category of all schemes, and in that case inclusion identifies these limits up to isomorphism; (4) the same condition holds for colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Here a limit is an object with compatible maps to the diagram through which every other such family factors uniquely. The underlying-category choice in the definition of a big fppf site means a choice of $S_0$ and $\alpha$ satisfying (1)--(4). As in the size convention, one may replace this category by a full skeleton: a full subcategory containing a representative of every isomorphism class. This definition specifies the admissibility condition on an already chosen category; it makes no assertion of existence of such a choice.
